examples.title: Rs 25,000 electronics purchase
examples.why: 1% base cashback with no cap: 25,000 x 1% = 250 (bank illustration).

examples.title: Rs 1,560 retail spend rounds down
examples.why: Cashback is rounded down per transaction: 1560 x 1% = 15.6 -> Rs 15 (bank example).

examples.title: Rs 3,000 fuel
examples.why: Fuel spends are on the not-eligible list.

examples.title: Rs 20,000 rent payment
examples.why: Rent payments are not eligible for cashback.

examples.title: Rs 2,000 wallet recharge
examples.why: Wallet recharge is not eligible for cashback.

examples.title: Rs 5,000 electricity bill NOT paid through Airtel Thanks
examples.why: Utility and telecom payments outside the Airtel Thanks app fall in no rewarded category (base 1% does not cover utility MCCs here).

examples.title: Rs 5,000 EMI purchase
examples.why: EMI transactions and post-facto EMI conversions earn no cashback.

examples.title: Rs 2,500 Airtel mobile bill via Airtel Thanks, no base spend this cycle
examples.why: T&C: "if customer does not spend any amount under Base category, the customer would not be eligible to earn cashback towards Airtel Bill payments made via Airtel Thanks platform". The 1% base does not cover this category.

examples.title: Rs 4,000 electricity bill via Airtel Thanks, no base spend this cycle
examples.why: T&C: the 10% utility category via Airtel Thanks is "capped at the base cashback earned during the statement month"; with no base spend nothing is earned, and the 1% base is for "all other spends" only.

examples.title: Bank illustration: Rs 2,500 Airtel mobile bill after Rs 250 base cashback this cycle
examples.why: Bank illustration: 25% of 2,500 = 625, capped at 2 x Rs 250 base cashback = 500.
examples.not_checkable_reason: The cap is a multiple of the cardholder's base cashback in the statement month (D13): not in the C3.1 context.

examples.title: Rs 1,000 Zomato order
examples.why: T&C, 10% value back on preferred merchants (Zomato, Blinkit, District): "Axis Bank cashback shall not be applicable for this category". The partner-wallet value back needs a coupon and is not card cashback here (info).

examples.title: Rs 300 highway toll
examples.why: T&C exclusion list: "Bridge Fees, Road Fees & Tolls".

research_notes.issuer_says: From 12 Apr 2026 (statements from 12 Jun 2026): 25% category is capped at 2x the base cashback earned in the statement month, 10% category at 1x. With no base spend there is no Airtel cashback. Bank illustration: base 250, Airtel mobile Rs 2,500 at 25% = 625 -> 500, utility Rs 4,000 at 10% = 400 -> 250.
research_notes.proposed_fix: engine: needs a cap whose amount is a multiple of base cashback earned in the period; until then the Airtel bonus rules should stay info-only (never ranked)

research_notes.issuer_says: 10% value back goes into the partner wallet (max Rs 200 per partner per month, min order Rs 499), with no Axis cashback. It is not card cashback.

research_notes.cardpipeline_says: accrual_engine.rounding_mode (points rounding field) used for a cashback card
research_notes.issuer_says: Cashback is rounded down per transaction (15.6 -> 15). (D11: cashback_rounding = rupee_floor; rounding_mode governs points only.)

research_notes.cardpipeline_says: accelerator rules with caps tied to base cashback
research_notes.issuer_says: The 25% and 10% Airtel Thanks rules depend on the cardholder base cashback earned in the month: rules set to info with flag depends_on_user_attribute; no entry-tier rate exists.

research_notes.item: Airtel Thanks, preferred merchants and exclusions (2026-11-06)
research_notes.cardpipeline_says: 25%/10% rules info; base 1% paid on Airtel Thanks bills and at Zomato/Blinkit; jewellery, tolls, cash/financial institutions, gift cards unmapped
research_notes.issuer_says: T&C (eff. 12 Apr 2026): 25%/10% capped at 2x/1x the month's base cashback, nothing without base spend; base 1% is for other spends only; "Axis Bank cashback shall not be applicable" on the preferred-merchant category; exclusion list includes Jewelry, Gift Cards, Bridge Fees, Road Fees & Tolls, Cash advances / Financial Institutions.
research_notes.proposed_fix: override: 25%/10% deferred (D13 depends_on_user_attribute), Airtel Thanks bills and Zomato/Blinkit/District excluded from base, value back deferred (coupon, D14b), MCC exclusions added
